purpose: Create unique, high-click, high-retention thumbnails for source-first American city-history videos where the active city is instantly recognizable, every public word is intentional, images are not distorted, and owner feedback blocks repeated weak patterns.
canonical_formula: Recognizable active-city skyline/landmark/place-specific hero + premium city typography + editorial art direction + intentional 2-4 word clear promise + one clear proof object or non-proof support object + verified spelling/OCR/safe-zone/no-distortion checks.

required_candidates.goal: Promise a clear active-city map or street transformation.
required_candidates.headline: {CITY} WAS REDRAWN

required_candidates.goal: Promise a clear hidden map or system explanation for the active city.
required_candidates.headline: {CITY_POSSESSIVE} HIDDEN MAP

required_candidates.goal: Promise a clear source-backed explanation of the active city contradiction.
required_candidates.headline: {CITY_POSSESSIVE} FALL EXPLAINED

pattern_lab_visual_requirements.city_anchor: The city must be instantly legible through skyline, street grid, neighborhood outline, landmark, factory, station, freeway, street sign, or map label.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.visual_contradiction: The image must show a tension such as old vs new, map line vs neighborhood, vanished building vs present void, or familiar myth vs source.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.proof_object: Include or imply a real source category: map, archival photo frame, dated document, building record, route line, neighborhood outline, or then/now frame.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.text_limit: Use 2-4 words. Never repeat the full title.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.title_pairing: The title completes the thumbnail promise; the thumbnail creates curiosity.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.first_30_second_payoff: The first 30 seconds of the video must show the exact map, source, place, or clue promised by the thumbnail.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.dominant_real_photo: Use one dominant rights-cleared photo, map, or document as the thumbnail base. Avoid collage unless it is a simple then/now split with one obvious question.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.human_or_action_interest: Prefer people, crowds, workers, transit, factories, attractions, demolition, street life, or other visible action over empty skyline or abstract source-board layouts.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.thumbnail_grading: Apply thumbnail-grade contrast: darker edges, brighter focal point, one bold accent color, strong text shadow, and no tiny explanatory labels.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.source_board_limit: Source proof must be implied by one clear proof object. Do not make the thumbnail look like an internal research board with many boxes, lines, or small labels.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.city_name_dominance: The active city name must be primary or co-primary text and must be understood as fast as the mystery phrase.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.search_result_shelf_test: Render a local YouTube search shelf with all five concepts and fail if the city name is weaker than benchmark examples or unclear without reading the title.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.competitive_color_contrast: Use competitive YouTube search-result contrast: yellow/white city text, one vivid accent, thick stroke/shadow, darker edges, and brighter focal point.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.five_concept_review: Generate five review concepts, then select the strongest three production candidates from that set.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.clear_thumbnail_promise: The text must make the likely video topic legible without reading the title. Ambiguous phrases like WAS REWIRED can only pass when upgraded to a clearer promise such as WAS REDRAWN or FALL EXPLAINED.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.premium_city_typography: Use Impact-style condensed display type, thick black stroke, drop shadow, warm yellow/orange fill, and slight 3D offset for the city name.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.competitive_benchmark_aesthetic: Match the competitive YouTube examples: large city text across the top, recognizable city/landmark visual, vivid accent, clean proof cue, and minimal clutter.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.polished_proof_mark: Use clean neon route/map arrows, silhouette-style marks, or proof cards. Avoid crude circles, giant X marks, and rough internal annotation marks.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.active_city_recognition: The base image must include a recognizable skyline, landmark, waterfront, station, factory, street grid, neighborhood outline, map label, route scar, or other place-specific visual anchor for the active city. Interior/tunnel/neighborhood-only images need skyline, landmark, map-label, or source-card pairing.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.ai_support_asset_boundary: AI may create non-evidence support graphics, background extensions, generic redacted documents, map textures, and reconstruction-style accents only when they are not presented as source proof and are logged for owner review.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.internet_reference_boundary: Do not clone or trace internet images that cannot be used. If a web image cannot be licensed, it may only inform a text description of generic composition, lighting, or mood; the generated output must be materially new, not a derivative copy, and cannot reproduce distinctive protected elements, watermarks, people, logos, or another creator thumbnail layout.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.owner_feedback_learning: Owner ratings under 4/10 are failing training data. Record the exact failure pattern and block repeated use of the same colors, labels, arrows, clutter, or image-placement mistake.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.every_word_earns_place: Every public word must either name the active city, clarify the curiosity hook, mark a simple time comparison, or create an intentional editorial prop. Filler labels and internal production terms fail the gate.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.spelling_and_ocr_verification: After rendering, OCR-readiness metadata must verify the active city spelling, expected headline words, and no cut-off text. Any misspelled city name or clipped headline blocks owner review.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.brightness_subject_visibility: The thumbnail must keep the focal image bright enough to understand at search-shelf size. Dark poster treatments may pass only when the text and focal proof object remain obvious.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.no_image_distortion: Images may be cropped, masked, graded, blurred, or extended; they must not be stretched or squeezed off-aspect. Then/now comparisons must preserve each source aspect ratio.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.layout_safe_zones: Keep primary words and important faces/landmarks away from edges and the lower-right YouTube timestamp zone. Overlays must adapt around the recognizable part of the city image.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.concept_specific_art_direction: Each thumbnail family has a style-specific checklist: redacted documents need readable sentences with selective redactions; newspapers need masthead/body columns/caption; underground concepts need real or generic underground imagery; then/now concepts need THEN left and NOW right unless the copy explicitly says otherwise.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.ai_generic_support: AI can generate generic non-evidence support objects such as underground tunnels, crowds, paper props, map textures, or lighting layers when rights-safe source photos are missing, but it must be logged as support and never represented as archival proof.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.creative_variation_memory: Future batches must not reuse the same composition, palette, proof-card placement, or title-bar lockup across all concepts. A batch must include meaningfully different editorial layouts.
pattern_lab_visual_requirements.per_thumbnail_critique: Every rendered thumbnail must include a critique record explaining the intended viewer reaction, why each word appears, why each image appears, what is emphasized, and known weaknesses.

design_constraints.mobile_readability: Must still read at small phone size.
design_constraints.composition: Recognizable active-city skyline/landmark/place-specific base, one source/proof card or polished proof cue, one large city lockup, strong contrast, no source-board clutter.
design_constraints.brand_style: Bright source-led editorial documentary: vivid cobalt or azure, warm gold/yellow, selective signal red, white type, near-black edge contrast, and restrained archival texture.
design_constraints.overlay_budget: Use at most one major proof mark: one arrow, route line, circle, tear, or split. Avoid multiple boxes, thin grids, and tiny labels.
design_constraints.photo_selection: Prefer beautiful, current, instantly recognizable skyline/landmark/current-city hero images first when they fit the promise; use older images as contrast/proof objects when the text promises before/old/year/vanished/fall. For any city, avoid generic interiors or anonymous streets unless paired with a city-specific skyline, landmark, map label, or dated source.
design_constraints.city_name_size: City text must be the primary/co-primary top type block in a premium display font.
design_constraints.search_shelf_readability: Test every review concept at reduced YouTube search-shelf size before owner review.
design_constraints.variant_pipeline: Generate 20 rough concepts, shortlist 8, render 5 owner-review concepts, and select 3 production candidates.
design_constraints.city_recognition: At least four of five review concepts must use skyline/landmark/place-specific recognition; all five must read as the active city through city text plus visual context.
design_constraints.text_word_intent: Every word must increase curiosity or clarity. Internal labels such as SOURCE PHOTO, PROOF, MAP PROOF, and SOURCE are banned unless the word is part of a viewer-facing promise.
design_constraints.arrow_rule: Arrows are banned by default. Allow a route/map arrow only when the video is literally about a route, movement, or map path and the arrow points to the proof object clearly.
design_constraints.text_intent_gate: Every word must pass a word-intent map before render. Ban decorative/filler words that do not raise curiosity or clarify the promise.
design_constraints.safe_zone_pixels: Primary text must stay at least 60 px from all edges and outside the lower-right timestamp danger zone unless intentionally part of a border/ticker element.
design_constraints.image_aspect_rule: Never distort source images. Use proportional cover/contain crop only.
design_constraints.brightness_rule: Require focal image visibility at reduced search-shelf size; avoid hiding the skyline/landmark under dark overlays.
design_constraints.publication_name_rule: Made-up newspaper names are allowed only as fictional props and require a pre-publication web search before any public thumbnail uses them.
design_constraints.redaction_rule: Redaction graphics must show partial readable sentence fragments plus selective black redactions, not rows of 100% black boxes.
design_constraints.then_now_rule: For then/now comparisons, THEN is left and NOW is right by default; source images must not be squeezed.
design_constraints.underground_rule: Underground concepts should use actual tunnel/underground/source imagery when available; generic AI/support imagery is allowed only if it cannot be verified as another city and is logged as non-proof support.

software_workflow.default_local_generation: OpenClaw creates deterministic city-recognizable competitive candidates from rights-cleared skyline/landmark/context photos plus proof cards, renders a search-shelf test, then selects production candidates; source-board graphics are support only, not the thumbnail look.
software_workflow.free_manual_editor: Photopea or GIMP for manual polish when local generation is not enough.
software_workflow.recommended_paid_editor: Canva Pro or Adobe Express Premium for fast premium layouts, brand templates, background removal, and resize workflows.
software_workflow.expert_editor: Photoshop/Affinity/Figma when a designer is manually building a reusable professional system.
software_workflow.youtube_testing: Use YouTube title/thumbnail A/B testing when available; pick winners by watch time, not CTR alone.
software_workflow.free_first_default: Use Canva Free, Photopea, GIMP, Upscayl, Google Fonts, LOC/Wikimedia/public archives, Tesseract/PaddleOCR, CLIP/OpenCLIP, SAM2/rembg before any paid service.
software_workflow.paid_escalation: Paid tools or paid assets require documented free-workflow failure plus explicit owner approval.
software_workflow.current_thumbnail_renderer: Current repo-local Pattern Lab thumbnail factory uses Swift/AppKit deterministic photo-backed compositing, not an AI image generator, for final thumbnail rendering.
software_workflow.recommended_free_ai_support_generator: Draw Things for interactive Apple-Silicon editing and ComfyUI for repeatable local workflows, using license-approved Qwen Image or FLUX-family models for non-proof support elements.
software_workflow.recommended_premium_ai_support_generator: OpenAI gpt-image-2 through OpenClaw image_generate for high-instruction-following support graphics/reference edits; use gpt-image-1.5 only when transparent-background cutouts are specifically needed.
software_workflow.recommended_llm_art_director: Use GPT-5.6 Terra reasoning/vision critique only at the 20-to-8, 8-to-5, and 5-to-3 checkpoints. Use local deterministic checks and local image models for routine work. Escalate once to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra only after two full cycles fail to produce a 90/100 candidate.
software_workflow.ai_support_asset_workflow: Use real licensed/current city hero images for the recognizable city layer. Use AI only to generate missing support layers: redacted-paper graphic, generic map texture, non-proof silhouette, background extension, clean tear/split, or atmospheric texture. Log prompt/model/reference and mark as support/reconstruction, never evidence.

recommended_autonomous_architecture.canonical_sequence: OpenClaw strategy/source safety -> Canva plugin render -> OpenClaw validation -> owner review / YouTube test
recommended_autonomous_architecture.openclaw_role: OpenClaw owns strategy, source safety, rights ledger checks, thumbnail briefs, title-thumbnail promise matching, validation, owner review packet, and YouTube testing notes.
recommended_autonomous_architecture.canva_role: Canva is the autonomous design/rendering engine when connected. Canva must not choose historical claims, override rights rules, or become the source of truth.
recommended_autonomous_architecture.owner_role: The owner remains final approver before private/unlisted upload and public publish.
recommended_autonomous_architecture.fallback: If Canva cannot produce a clean policy-compliant export, OpenClaw must fall back to local generation plus Photopea/GIMP polish.

canva_renderer_policy.role: Canva is the design/rendering engine. OpenClaw remains responsible for concept, source safety, rights ledger checks, title-thumbnail promise matching, and validation.
canva_renderer_policy.canva_free_rule: Canva Free is acceptable when the design uses user-uploaded assets, free templates/elements, no Pro-locked media, and exports clean PNG/JPG without watermark.
canva_pro_recommended_when: background removal or advanced cutout work is needed
brand kit/template consistency saves production time
premium templates or stock elements materially improve quality
Magic Resize or faster multi-format export is needed
OpenClaw cannot produce an excellent thumbnail with free/local tools
canva_renderer_policy.plugin_instruction: When the Canva plugin is available, generate a structured Canva brief for five active-city-recognizable competitive review concepts, use a premium city typography treatment, export the selected PNG/JPG thumbnails, save outputs locally, and record the Canva design URL or id in the review packet.
canva_renderer_policy.fallback_instruction: If Canva export fails, uses Pro-locked assets, adds watermarking, or cannot meet the policy checks, fall back to local OpenClaw generation plus Photopea/GIMP manual polish.
hard_reject: Pro-locked element in a Free-plan export
template that looks generic or copied
design not exportable as a clean image file
thumbnail not reproducible from logged source media and brief

hard_blocks: generic AI cityscape
fake archival photo
misleading claim not paid off in first 30 seconds
text over 4 words unless owner explicitly approves
collage with too many competing focal points
low contrast or unreadable phone-size text
source or rights unclear
watermarked stock image
copied thumbnail layout from another channel
shock face or cheap clickbait inconsistent with Pattern Lab brand
empty skyline-only visual without a specific contradiction
source-board clutter or internal research-board look
thin map lines or boxes that become noise at phone size
tiny source labels that cannot be read on a phone
more than one competing focal point
city only a small tag
city name unreadable at phone size
missing local thumbnail search shelf test
weak city text compared with benchmark search-result examples
ambiguous thumbnail promise
boring/plain city font
not recognizably the active city
rough proof marks or crude X/circle annotations
missing skyline or landmark recognition when source assets are available
paid tool used without owner approval
paid asset used without owner approval
AI output copied from an unlicensed reference image
AI-generated city hero image used when a rights-safe real city hero image is available
AI-generated support element presented as source proof
internal label such as SOURCE, SOURCE PHOTO, PROOF, or MAP PROOF on the public thumbnail
random arrow not tied to a route/map/path promise
repeating an owner-rated sub-4/10 failure pattern without redesign
THEN/NOW comparison with NOW on the left unless explicitly justified
THEN/NOW comparison that pairs a map with a photograph
map used as a substitute for a required historical photograph
background too dark to understand at search-shelf size
dim or visually flat hero image when a brighter crop or source is available
generic rounded black text card as the primary readability treatment
cut-off thumbnail text
fake newspaper without body text/columns/caption when presented as newspaper style
made-up publication name used publicly without pre-publication web/name-conflict check
misspelled active city name
overlays covering the recognizable skyline, landmark, face, or proof object
redaction graphic with only solid black boxes and no readable sentence context
reusing the same title-bar/proof-card layout across all five concepts
stretched or squeezed source image
unintentional public words or filler labels
redrawn thumbnail using only a generic skyline when a rights-clear map or street grid is available
hidden/under-city thumbnail without tunnel, sewer, subway, utility, or hidden-system visual support
partial-word redactions
low-value public labels such as REDACTED CITY FILE
rail or track-only image used for a lost-streets promise
then/now image crossing the center divider
NOW-side image that is dark, old-looking, distorted, or not current city context
AI support asset presented as source proof or archival evidence

city_name_policy.rule: The active city name must be primary or co-primary text in a premium condensed display treatment, not a small badge, label, or afterthought.
city_name_policy.font_rule: Use local Impact when present; fallback to Arial Black/Arial Bold only with a report warning.
city_name_policy.phone_size_requirement: The city name and promise must remain readable in a YouTube search-result shelf and on a phone without reading the video title.
city_name_policy.hard_block: Block any thumbnail where the active city is only a small tag, the promise is ambiguous, or the visual does not read as that city.
city_name_policy.identity_source: Exact episode package and upload metadata must agree; no title parsing or policy fallback.

city_agnostic.template_rule: Use explicit {CITY}, {CITY_POSSESSIVE}, and episode-owned {YEAR} placeholders for every city. No city-specific workflow rule or fallback is allowed.
city_agnostic.thumbnail_city_rule: The active city name must be the primary or co-primary visual product for every city, not a small tag.
city_agnostic.episode_specific_override_rule: Every episode package must provide exactly five topic-specific concepts with these concept IDs. Generic templates are schema examples only and may not be rendered for owner review.

redacted_file.example_sentence_template: The {CITY} route was approved in 1942, then [REDACTED] before construction began.

newspaper_front_page.pre_publication_requirement: Search the web before public use to verify the fictional masthead is not an active/confusing real newspaper name.

required: active city is the attention word
secondary color does not steal attention
generic support asset logged if not city-specific
underground_city.city_specificity_rule: Generic underground support imagery is acceptable only when it cannot be verified as another city and is not presented as source evidence.

required: one simple support object or none

concept_specific_rules.redrawn_map_semantic_match: Redrawn concepts must use a city map, street grid, highway map, or map/photo hybrid when available.
concept_specific_rules.underground_semantic_asset: Hidden-map/under-city concepts must use tunnel, sewer, subway, utility, or hidden-system imagery; generic AI support is non-proof only.
concept_specific_rules.whole_word_redaction: Redacted document concepts must redact whole words only and keep readable sentence fragments.
concept_specific_rules.curiosity_hook_prominence: The curiosity hook, such as WHO ERASED IT?, must be visibly prominent and more important than administrative prop labels.
concept_specific_rules.lost_streets_visual_relevance: Lost-streets concepts must use streets, road grids, maps, city blocks, demolition/voids, or old street photos; rail-only photos are blocked.
concept_specific_rules.then_now_split_integrity: Then/now concepts must keep THEN on the left, NOW on the right, with no source image crossing the center divider.
concept_specific_rules.current_style_renderer_v4: Prefer the owner-rated current workflow baseline for normal review batches; defer outside-the-box tournament formats until explicitly requested.
